checks.title: Validate Call ID Format (A999)
checks.rationale: Ensures that the primary identifier for the call event conforms to the expected internal naming convention derived from the pattern samples ('A999'). Consistency is crucial for joins and indexing.
checks.assumption: The 'call_id' follows a strict format of one uppercase letter followed by three digits.

checks.title: Caller MSISDN Length Check
checks.rationale: Mobile Station International Subscriber Directory Numbers (MSISDNs) typically fall within a standard length range (10-15 digits) globally. Values outside this range suggest data corruption or incorrect masking.
checks.assumption: MSISDNs in this dataset, even if masked, represent standard mobile phone numbers requiring 10 to 15 characters.

checks.title: Callee MSISDN Must Not Be Null (Low Tolerance)
checks.rationale: A Call Detail Record (CDR) must typically have both a caller and a callee. A 10% null rate for 'callee_msisdn' is high and suggests missing destination information, which is critical for billing and network analysis.
checks.assumption: The destination number ('callee_msisdn') is mandatory for a valid call record.

checks.title: Callee MSISDN Length Check (Addressing Length 5 Anomaly)
checks.rationale: The profile shows a suspicious length of 5 for 'callee_msisdn'. Assuming this is an artifact of masking or bad data, this check enforces a realistic length range consistent with standard MSISDNs (10-15 characters), similar to the caller field.
checks.assumption: Both caller and callee MSISDNs should adhere to similar standard phone number length requirements.

checks.title: Call Start Time Must Not Be In The Future
checks.rationale: Ensures that all recorded events have occurred in the past, preventing ingestion of records with incorrect system timestamps or future dates.
checks.assumption: All records represent historical call events.

checks.title: Validate Call Start Time ISO 8601 UTC Format
checks.rationale: Ensures the timestamp field adheres strictly to the expected ISO 8601 format ending in 'Z' (Zulu/UTC), which is critical for time series analysis and cross-system compatibility.
checks.assumption: The 'call_start_utc' column uses the standard ISO 8601 format for UTC timestamps.

checks.title: Call Duration Must Be Non-Negative
checks.rationale: Physical duration cannot be negative. The profile shows a minimum value of -30, indicating data corruption or an error in logging/processing.
checks.assumption: Call duration must be zero or positive.

checks.title: Detect Extreme Outliers in Call Duration
checks.rationale: Identifies extremely long calls (e.g., sessions left open) that might skew aggregate statistics or indicate system errors, especially given the high maximum value (999999 seconds).
checks.assumption: Call durations follow a distribution where extreme values (3.0 * IQR beyond quartiles) are likely anomalies.

checks.title: Monitor New Call Types
checks.rationale: Ensures that new, unexpected categories (beyond VOICE, SMS, DATA) are flagged, as they might require updates to downstream processing or billing logic.
checks.assumption: The set of valid 'call_type' values is relatively stable, and new values should be reviewed.

checks.title: Validate Cell Tower ID Format
checks.rationale: Ensures the cell tower identifier adheres to the expected internal structure (e.g., 'TWR-XXXX'), which is vital for network analysis and location tracking.
checks.assumption: Cell tower IDs follow the format 'TWR-' followed by four digits.

checks.title: Validate Country Code Against Expected Set
checks.rationale: Ensures the country code is one of the expected ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 codes relevant to the telecom operator's service area.
checks.assumption: The dataset primarily covers India ('IN') but should allow for a small set of valid, known country codes.

checks.title: Charge Amount Must Be Non-Negative
checks.rationale: Billing charges should typically be zero or positive. Negative charges usually indicate refunds or errors, which should be explicitly monitored if they occur frequently.
checks.assumption: This field represents a charge, not a credit/refund, and must be non-negative.

checks.title: Validate Currency Code Against Expected Set
checks.rationale: Ensures the currency code is a valid ISO 4217 code and matches the expected currencies used for billing.
checks.assumption: The primary currency is INR, but a few other major currencies might be expected for international calls.

checks.title: Zero Duration Implies Zero Charge
checks.rationale: If a call or session lasted zero seconds (e.g., failed connection, missed call), it should generally not incur a charge. This checks for billing errors where zero-duration events are charged.
checks.assumption: Billing logic dictates that events with zero duration must have a zero charge amount.

checks.title: Charged Call Must Have Non-Negative Duration
checks.rationale: If a charge is applied (charge_amount > 0), the associated duration must logically be non-negative. This specifically catches the negative duration issue identified in the profile when linked to billing.
checks.assumption: Any charged event must have a duration greater than or equal to zero.
